class.name: MultiMeshBulletsData2D
class.description: Shared base for [DirectionalBulletsData2D] and [BlockBulletsData2D]. Fill in [member transforms] (mandatory, one per bullet), a [member sprite_frames] animation, collision settings, lifetime, and optional rotation, material, and custom data, then hand it to a [BulletFactory2D] spawn method. The same resource can be reused for every volley.

method.name: calculate_bitmask
method.description: Calculates a bitmask from an array of integers.

method.name: set_collision_layer_from_array
method.description: Sets the collision layer from an array of integers by converting them to a bitmask.

method.name: set_collision_mask_from_array
method.description: Sets the collision mask from an array of integers by converting them to a bitmask.

method.name: set_light_mask_from_array
method.description: Sets the light mask from an array of integers by converting them to a bitmask.

method.name: set_visibility_layer_from_array
method.description: Sets the visibility layers from an array of integers by converting them to a bitmask.

members.member: Spin for each bullet. Entry [code]i[/code] rotates bullet [code]i[/code] only — give one entry per bullet (same size as [member transforms]), or leave empty for no rotation. Bullets without a valid entry read zero spin (or the [DirectionalBulletsData2D.shared_bullet_rotation_data] fallback on Directional volleys). Invalid means: null entry, or NaN/Inf rotation values (that bullet reads zeros, its siblings are untouched). Example: entries [2.0, null] → bullet 0 spins at 2.0, bullet 1 holds still. Note: [BulletRotationData2D] has a helper static method that you can use to generate random rotation data - [method BulletRotationData2D.generate_random_data].
When on, a short [member all_bullet_rotation_data] wraps around the volley (bullet [code]i[/code] reads entry [code]i % size[/code]) instead of leaving the tail bullets at zero spin. Off by default.

Custom data carried per bullet, readable in the factory collision callbacks through [method MultiMeshBullets2D.bullet_get_custom_data]. Entry [code]i[/code] belongs to bullet [code]i[/code] and nobody else; bullets without an entry read null. Stays strictly separate from [member shared_bullets_custom_data]: per-bullet data never falls back to shared. Example: tag bullet 0 with a fire resource and bullet 2 with ice → bullet 1 reads null.
When on, a short [member all_bullets_custom_data] wraps around the volley instead of leaving the tail bullets at null. Off by default.

Which SpriteFrames animation to play. Empty or "default" auto-resolves silently ("default" if present, else first animation). Explicit wrong names fall back to the first animation with one error. The whole multimesh batch shares one frame at a time; timing uses animation speed (fps), per-frame durations, and loop flag.
How many times a bullet can collide before it gets disabled. If you set to 0, then the bullet will NEVER get disabled due to collisions.

Starting hit count for each bullet. Entry [code]i[/code] belongs to bullet [code]i[/code]; bullets without an entry start at 0. Leave empty to start every bullet fresh. Values are clamped into range (negatives become 0, values at or above [member bullet_max_collision_count] become max - 1, exactly one hit remaining, when the max is above 0).
When on, a short [member bullets_current_collision_count] wraps around the volley instead of starting the tail bullets at 0. Off by default.

The bitmask for the collision layer.
Note: Needs to be set to a bitmask, so use [method calculate_bitmask]. Tip: [method set_collision_layer_from_array] takes plain layer numbers and builds the bitmask for you.

The bitmask for the collision mask.
Note: Needs to be set to a bitmask, so use [method calculate_bitmask]. Tip: [method set_collision_mask_from_array] takes plain layer numbers and builds the bitmask for you.

The collision shape shared by all bullets in the multimesh. Supports [RectangleShape2D], [CircleShape2D] and [CapsuleShape2D]; anything else falls back to a circle with an error. The effective type is part of the pool bucket, so changing it changes which pooled instances get reused. Use [member collision_shape_offset] to shift it away from the texture center, and enable the [BulletFactory2D] debugger to see it.

The offset for the collision shape calculated from the center of the bullet texture.
Note: You can enable the [BulletFactory2D]'s debugger to make collision shapes visible.

Per-instance shader overrides, used only when [member material] is a [ShaderMaterial] with [code]instance uniform[/code] declarations. [b]KEY[/b] is the uniform name ([String]), [b]VALUE[/b] is a [Variant] matching that uniform's type (a wrong type warns and skips that key). Applied per bullet instance through [code]set_instance_shader_parameter()[/code] when the volley spawns every live bullet of the multimesh shares the same override set. An empty dictionary disables the pass. Switching to a non-shader material, or spawning with null material, clears the stored dict so pool reuse never leaks stale overrides into the next volley. Example: assign a [ShaderMaterial] with [code]instance uniform vec4 glow_color[/code] and set this to [code]{"glow_color": Color(1, 0.3, 0.1, 1)}[/code]. Global (non-instance) uniforms belong on the material itself, not here.

If you set to true, then the lifetime will be ignored and bullets will never be destroyed.
Warning: If you don't implement "collision walls" or anything else to intercept/collide with the bullets, then they will truly live forever in your memory and you will experience lag. Warning: When using unit curves with [BulletCurvesData2D] they might not work properly.

If this is enabled then when the lifetime of the bullets is over, the signal [signal BulletFactory2D.directional_life_time_over] (or [signal BulletFactory2D.block_life_time_over]) will be emitted by the [BulletFactory2D]. This is helpful when you want to spawn visual effects at that time (explosion, particles, anything really..).

By default the texture is always rotated to match the bullet's transform rotation. This property disables that behavior and ensures that the bullet is always spawned rotated based on [member texture_rotation_radians] only.

The bitmask for the light mask.
Note: Needs to be set to a bitmask, so use [method calculate_bitmask]. Tip: [method set_light_mask_from_array] takes plain layer numbers and builds the bitmask for you.

Bullet material. Pick a [ShaderMaterial] (use [member instance_shader_parameters] for per-volley instance uniforms) or a [CanvasItemMaterial]. Null uses the default canvas material. The inspector filters to these two types.
The max time before the bullets get disabled and go in the object pool.

Custom bullet mesh. If null (default) a [QuadMesh] is auto-built from [member texture_size] (or the first animation frame size). Provide your own [Mesh] only when you handle scaling in the shader. The inspector filters to [Mesh] resources.

If you want static bodies to be hit by the bullets, you have to set [member monitorable] to true.
Note: This is at the cost of performance, so a better workaround is to attach an [Area2D] to those static bodies and detect that instead.

If you set this to [code]false[/code], then the collision shapes will also rotate along with the bullet's texture.
Note: You can enable the [BulletFactory2D]'s debugger to make collision shapes visible.

Shared attachment scene applied to every bullet at spawn time (and on pool reuse). The scene must contain a [BulletAttachment2D]. Null (default) disables the feature; use the runtime [method MultiMeshBullets2D.bullet_set_attachment] methods for per-bullet attachments instead.
Offset of the shared attachment relative to the bullet's texture center.
Whether the shared attachment sticks while the bullet rotates.

If you want your bullets to have damage or any other data specific to this type of bullets then you have to provide a custom resource that holds all of these properties. Any [Resource] subclass works (script custom classes included); read it back in factory collision callbacks alongside [member all_bullets_custom_data].
[url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fdRJqnOrz98&t=63s]YouTube Tutorial On Custom Resources[/url]
SpriteFrames holding all animations. Each frame is a Texture2D (plain or AtlasTexture region). The batch shares one frame; per-frame duration and loop come from the animation.
Set this to true if you want for the bullets to stop rotating when they reach the maximum rotation speed.
If your texture is not rotated properly, you can use this property to rotate it more.
QuadMesh size override, used only when no mesh is provided. If x/y <= 0 the size auto-derives from the first frame (AtlasTexture region, else texture size).

[b]MANDATORY[/b] Determines the transforms of the bullets, in global space (use each marker's global transform). Movement, physics shapes, collision signals and [method MultiMeshBullets2D.get_bullet_global_transform] all operate in global space.
Tip: place [Marker2D] nodes in your scene and read their global transforms each time you spawn. Note: There is a helper static function that can generate a grid pattern of [Transform2D] that you can use: [method BulletFactory2D.helper_generate_transforms_grid]. You might want to implement your own custom pattern generation logic in C++ for maximum performance.

The bitmask for the visibility layer.
Note: Needs to be set to a bitmask, so use [method calculate_bitmask]. Tip: [method set_visibility_layer_from_array] takes plain layer numbers and builds the bitmask for you.
The z index of the bullets.
